items.title: Meet Yuan Chen - Speaker at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America
items.author: CNCF [Cloud Native Computing Foundation]
items.content:
<article>Every cloud brings different GPU taints, plugins, storage classes and annotations. Yuan Chen of NVIDIA is heading to KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America to share a more portable approach.

Learn how a criteria-driven recipe model can generate Helm bundles across five cloud environments and create a queryable audit layer for platform teams, SREs and FinOps practitioners.

Join us November 9-12 in Salt Lake City.

Explore the session: https://bit.ly/4rUZXXH

Register: https://bit.ly/3BDI5XL</article>

items.title: Meet Andy Anderson - Speaker at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America
items.author: CNCF [Cloud Native Computing Foundation]
items.content:
<article>What happens when autonomous agents become part of an open source maintenance crew?

At KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America, Andy Anderson of IBM Research will share how KubeStellar Console merged roughly 2,400 pull requests across 211 releases in just 90 days, including approximately 850 opened by autonomous agents.

Learn what these agents handle well, where they stumble, and what their work changes for project maintainers.

Join us November 9-12 in Salt Lake City.

Register: https://bit.ly/3BDI5XL</article>

items.title: Behind every open source project is a global community willing to share what they learn
items.author: CNCF [Cloud Native Computing Foundation]
items.content:
<article>Kubestronaut Mahendran Selvakumar highlights why direct, face-to-face collaboration is the heart of KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America. The real power of the cloud native ecosystem comes from the hallway conversations, technical exchanges, and personal connections formed between project maintainers, organizers, and contributors.

Meet the organizers, maintainers, and builders in person. Join us in shaping the future of open source systems.

Register for KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America: https://bit.ly/4z2FJO6

#Kubestronaut #CloudNative #Kubernetes #OpenSource #KubeCon</article>

items.title: Meet Abby Bangser + Phill Morton - Speakers at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America
items.author: CNCF [Cloud Native Computing Foundation]
items.content:
<article>What gives cloud native its greatest advantage? The community that builds it.

Abby Bangser, Principal Engineer at Syntasso, and Phill Morton, Platform Architect at The Access Group, will present the keynote “The Flywheel Effect: Why Community Is the Ultimate End-User Advantage” at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America.

Discover how shared experience, open collaboration, and end-user contributions help organizations solve problems faster and turn community ideas into practical platforms.

Join us November 9-12 in Salt Lake City.

Explore Abby & Phill’s session: https://bit.ly/4y3VK5t

Register: https://bit.ly/3BDI5XL</article>

items.title: How do you stay connected to the global cloud native community?
items.author: CNCF [Cloud Native Computing Foundation]
items.content:
<article>CNCF Ambassador Wendy Ha shares what KubeCon + CloudNativeCon means to her, from discovering real-world production use cases and emerging tooling to building strong connections with contributors around the world.

KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America brings together 9,000+ maintainers, platform teams, and infrastructure engineers for four days of deep technical learning and community connection. Explore over 400 sessions, co-located events like Cloud Native AI + Inference Day, and hands-on discussions on building reliable platforms at scale.

Save your seat and connect with the global community in person: https://bit.ly/4z2FJO6

#CloudNative #KubeCon</article>

items.title: Meet Kashif Khan - Speaker at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America
items.author: CNCF [Cloud Native Computing Foundation]
items.content:
<article>Join Kashif Khan, Co-Chair of CNCF TAG Infrastructure, Metal3 maintainer, Open Source Architect at Ericsson, at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America, November 9-12 in Salt Lake City, Utah.

In “Beyond Provisioning: Multi-Tenancy, Rack Awareness, and Declarative Networking in Metal3,” Kashif and Sunnatillo Samadov will demonstrate how Metal3 can help teams share hardware securely, spread control plane nodes across racks, and automate physical network configuration through Kubernetes APIs.

Kashif will also present a Metal3 Project Lightning Talk and join “Cloud Native Infrastructure in the AI Era: A TAG Infrastructure Panel.”

Explore Kashif’s sessions:
https://bit.ly/4dPe4bm

Register:
https://bit.ly/3BDI5XL</article>

items.title: Cloud Native Live: Compliance at Scale with Kyverno - Razorpay and Nirmata
items.author: CNCF [Cloud Native Computing Foundation]
items.content:
<article>Razorpay processes over $180 billion in payments annually and powers 80 of India’s top 100 unicorns. Operating at this scale in a regulated financial market means meeting strict Reserve Bank of India (RBI) requirements while maintaining 99.99% system availability and releasing new features quickly.

In this fireside chat, Ashwath Kumar (Head of Security at Razorpay) and Jim Bugwadia (CEO at Nirmata) share how Razorpay automated its security policies. By adopting Kyverno Razorpay moved from manual audits to continuous, automated compliance across its entire infrastructure. They will also discuss how active involvement in the CNCF community.</article>

items.title: Meet Norwin Schnyder - Speaker at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America
items.author: CNCF [Cloud Native Computing Foundation]
items.content:
<article>Join Norwin Schnyder, Senior Cloud Software Engineer at Airlock, at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America, November 9-12 in Salt Lake City, Utah.

Explore new work across HTTPRoute, TCP and UDP integration, flexible backend policies, AI and agentic traffic patterns, and the Gateway API roadmap.

https://bit.ly/4dRjLWc

items.title: Why do over 9,000 tech professionals gather at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon?
items.author: CNCF [Cloud Native Computing Foundation]
items.content:
<article>It comes down to community connection and direct access to the maintainers building open infrastructure.

Haleema Khan shares her experience attending and why in-person knowledge exchange is essential for technical growth. From comparing open approaches in GPU scheduling and model serving to connecting with platform teams operating at scale, the real-world insights gained face-to-face cannot be replicated online.

Register today: https://bit.ly/4z2FJO6

#KubeCon #PlatformEngineering #OpenSource</article>

items.title: Better together in open source
items.author: CNCF [Cloud Native Computing Foundation]
items.content:
<article>Cloud native practitioner Bailey Hayes explains why contributing to community projects gives her confidence to build.

Sustainable software development relies on collective collaboration. Having a dedicated global community behind open source tools gives engineering teams the security and confidence to innovate.

Hear real-world insights from builders shaping open source. Join us in person by registering for KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America: https://bit.ly/4z2FJO6

#CNCF #CloudNative #OpenSource #KubeCon #DeveloperCommunity</article>

items.title: Meet Qasim Sarfraz - Speaker at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America
items.author: CNCF [Cloud Native Computing Foundation]
items.content:
<article>Join Qasim Sarfraz, Software Engineer at Microsoft, at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America, November 9-12 in Salt Lake City, Utah.

In “GPU Observability with eBPF: From Kernel Hooks to Kubernetes Metrics,” Qasim and Maya Singh will explore how eBPF can provide visibility into GPU workloads without modifying application code.

Learn how to connect GPU activity with Kubernetes context, package eBPF programs as portable OCI images, and send GPU telemetry to Prometheus and OpenTelemetry.

Qasim will also appear in an Inspektor Gadget Project Lightning Talk and a hands-on Contribfest session.

Explore Qasim’s sessions:
https://bit.ly/4he08Kb 

Register:
https://bit.ly/3BDI5XL</article>

items.title: ChatLoopBackOff Episode 82: SlimFaas with Thomas and Guillaume
items.author: CNCF [Cloud Native Computing Foundation]
items.content: <article>Join CNCF Ambassador Thomas Schuetz as he explores SlimFaas for the first time in this interactive ChatLoopBackOff session. items.title: Beyond protoc --decode: Schema Inference, Lossless Decoding, and... Frederic Ruget, S3NS
items.author: CNCF [Cloud Native Computing Foundation]
items.content:
<article>Don't miss out! Join us at our next KubeCon + CloudNativeCon event in Salt Lake City, United States (Nov 9–12, 2026). Connect with our current graduated, incubating, and sandbox projects as the community gathers to further the education and advancement of cloud native computing. Learn more at https://kubecon.io

Beyond protoc --decode: Schema Inference, Lossless Decoding, and Descriptor Archaeology - Frederic Ruget, S3NS (Thales × Google Cloud)

Every gRPC engineer eventually faces a binary .pb blob of unknown type, a compiled descriptor with no .proto source, or an editions descriptor a downstream toolchain cannot consume. Standard tooling stops short: protoc --decode requires the original descriptor and exact type name, silently discards non-canonical bytes, crashes on malformed input.

prototools is a pair of open-source CLI tools that fill this gap.

prototext decodes binary protobuf with or without a schema. Given a descriptor DB, it automatically infers the message type — ranking all candidates from a corpus of thousands of types in seconds. It also preserves every non-canonical byte via inline annotations and round-trips byte-exact, even for malformed protobufs.

reproto reconstructs compilable .proto source files from any FileDescriptorSet, handling proto2, proto3, and editions. It also builds the indexed descriptor databases that power prototext's auto-inference.

The talk is built around a live terminal demo.</article>
